summary: Today’s pulse tracks USS Lincoln returning to San Diego after record time at sea as families gather to greet crew – live, Suicide is up among Black Americans. We need to talk about it, and Microsoft suspended from applying for green cards for H-1B workers, JD Vance says. Across Guardian, NPR, and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are accused, workers, and goldman. In the background, Adidas sues Australian label White Fox over four stripes design and Royal Navy sailor accused of spying for Russia appears in court keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: USS Lincoln returning to San Diego after record time at sea as families gather to greet crew – live
headlines.description: Aircraft carrier making its way to port after 260 days at sea led to mental health crisis that made global headlines On Truth Social, Trump described Paxton as “ready, willing, and able” to take on Talarico – the 37-year-old state representative who has been leading in several polls. In Georgia, Jon Ossoff , the Democratic incumbent will face off against Mike Collins – a congressman and the Trump-backed Republican nominee at 7pm ET. At the same time in Michigan, progressive insurgent Abdul El-Sayed , will debate Mike Rogers , the Republican nominee also endorsed by the president. Finally, it’s the second debate in Maine in as many days. Susan Collins , the five-term Republican incumbent will spar (again) with the Democratic nominee, Troy Jackson , at 8pm ET.

headlines.title: Suicide is up among Black Americans. We need to talk about it.
headlines.description: NPR's Michel Martin hosted a panel conversation about mental health and suicide in the Black community, exploring a difficult subject in deeply personal conversations.

headlines.title: Microsoft suspended from applying for green cards for H-1B workers, JD Vance says
headlines.description: Vice-president also says Adobe is barred from visa program that allows high-skilled workers to apply for US residency Microsoft is suspended from applying for permanent residency for workers employed through a US visa program for high-skilled workers, JD Vance announced on Thursday. The US vice-president accused the tech company of abusing the H-1B system, which allows those on the visa to work while they apply and are in process for a green card.

headlines.title: Adidas sues Australian label White Fox over four stripes design
headlines.description: The German sportswear brand wants the Sydney-based label to stop selling the clothes and pay damages.

headlines.title: Royal Navy sailor accused of spying for Russia appears in court
headlines.description: Intelligence specialist Teddy Young, 24, alleged to have drafted message in Russian containing classified information A junior Royal Navy intelligence specialist from Bedfordshire accused of trying to pass military secrets to Russia appeared in court on Thursday. Teddy Young, 24, was accused of abusing his high-level security clearance to access secret defence and intelligence data after being deployed on a warship.

headlines.title: Top bosses at Goldman Sachs to share bonus pot worth up to $500m
headlines.description: Eye-watering sum, to be split between 20 bankers, is one of the biggest payouts in the bank’s history Top bosses at Goldman Sachs are in line to share a bonus pot worth up to $500m (£378m) this year, marking one of the biggest payouts in the Wall Street bank’s history. The eye-watering sum will be shared between 20 bankers, with its chief executive, David Solomon, due to take about $100m (£75.6m) of the reward, which is made up of Goldman Sachs stock.

headlinePool.title: Nicolás Maduro and his wife indicted for alleged torture of US citizens
headlinePool.description: Ousted Venezuelan president and Cilia Flores have been in jail in New York since early January The deposed Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, have been indicted for alleged conspiracy to commit torture, according to Manhattan federal court papers unsealed on Thursday. The superseding indictment was unsealed shortly before Flores appeared at court in her ongoing push for pre-trial release – which was denied by Judge Alvin Hellerstein. Maduro and Flores have jailed in New York City since early January.

headlinePool.title: Astronomers detect mysterious burst of energy from a galaxy far, far away
headlinePool.description: Intense flash of radio waves is more than 10bn years old and has travelled through ‘approximately 80% of cosmic history’ A long time ago in a galaxy far, far away, a mysterious flash of energy was released into the universe. Astronomers have now detected that flash, a burst of radio waves which travelled for more than 10bn years before reaching Earth – what they believe to be the most distant fast radio burst (FRB) ever recorded.

headlinePool.title: Trump made ‘clear’ that media ban was due to critical coverage, court told
headlinePool.description: Lawyer for CNN, MS Now and Politico says Trump admitted he banned networks from White House over their coverage Donald Trump continues to be the strongest witness for the media companies arguing that they were unfairly barred from the White House at his direction, a lawyer representing CNN, MS Now and Politico told a federal judge on Thursday afternoon. The media coalition was in court asking the judge to extend the temporary restraining order (TRO) he issued on 24 September requiring the White House to lift the ban for 14 days. That temporary reprieve was scheduled to expire on Thursday, but district court judge Timothy Kelly, a Trump appointee, said he would extend it until Tuesday and that he would probably rule on a motion for a preliminary injunction by that day. That means the White House will be forced to allow journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico to continue accessing the building until at least Tuesday.

headlinePool.title: Marco Rubio brushes off questions about Kimberly Guilfoyle pressing donor to pay credit card
headlinePool.description: US ambassador to Greece allegedly asked Trump donor to pay $100,000 American Express bill Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, brushed off reporters’ questions about recent reports that Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US ambassador to Greece and Trump family ally, used her position to advance personal interests. Rubio refused to respond to the latest allegations against Guilfoyle, raised in a Wall Street Journal report , claiming she asked a Trump donor to pay her $100,000 American Express bill in exchange for access to the administration, before her US Senate confirmation hearing.

headlinePool.title: Israel promotes film that mimics NAZA documentary
headlinePool.description: Embassies post links to hastily produced online film echoing style of real Guardian documentary about mass killings of Gaza civilians The Israeli government is promoting an online film project that mimics the style of NAZA, the award-winning documentary that details Israel’s mass killings of civilians in Gaza, in an attempt to counter the real film’s findings. The real documentary , directed by the Oscar-winning film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, and produced by the Guardian, is in cinemas and will be shown in more than 50 countries.

headlinePool.title: French students continue protests, saying ministers’ pledges not enough
headlinePool.description: Schools blockaded again across country as teenagers and teachers demand more investment and ‘concrete measures’ to improve conditions High school students have again blockaded schools and marched through cities across France, promising to continue their campaign despite government pledges to address the grievances underlying 10 days of protests that have left hundreds injured. Large crowds took to the streets on Thursday for mainly peaceful demonstrations in cities including Lille, Rennes, Nantes, Lyon, Toulon and Marseille, while in Paris a large procession marched through the city centre to the Place de la Bastille.

headlinePool.title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture
headlinePool.description: The new accusations relate to the alleged torture of US citizens held in Venezuela while Maduro was in power.

headlinePool.title: Two Latvian men arrested at RAF base in Cambridgeshire used by US military
headlinePool.description: Men aged 32 and 36 detained on suspicion of trespass, causing criminal damage and entering a prohibited place Two Latvian men were arrested in the early hours of Thursday after they were discovered inside the perimeter of RAF Molesworth, a Cambridgeshire base used by the US military and Nato for intelligence operations. The men, 32 and 36, were picked up at 2am inside the base, in an investigation that began four hours earlier when military police discovered an abandoned vehicle outside the facility.

headlinePool.title: What would make your life easier? Martin Lewis asks public for ‘small ideas’ to improve UK
headlinePool.description: Finance expert launches Small Ideas Initiative to gather ‘practical, low-cost’ ideas to put before cross-party panel Every day, people run into what the finance expert Martin Lewis calls “the life-potholes of unintended consequences” – clunky systems and poorly conceived rules that make life harder than it should be. His latest project, the Small Ideas Initiative , will attempt to address that, with a cross-party panel of politicians and policymakers crowdsourcing ideas for everyday fixes to take to government. The ideas could cover anything from health and schools to policing, tech and money. Lewis is encouraging people to submit ideas for “practical, low-cost, non-controversial ways to improve the UK” before 12 November.
